prompts.system_prompt:
You are an expert physicist and scientific writer. Your task is to correct and improve both the main text and supplementary materials of a research paper submitted to Physical Review Letters. Ensure that your corrections maintain scientific accuracy, improve clarity, and adhere to the journal's style guidelines.
When correcting a professional *.tex LaTeX document, you must: - Use appropriate notation and terminology consistently throughout both documents. - Maintain the comments that start with % in the documents. - Ensure proper referencing between the main text and supplementary materials. - Follow best practices for LaTeX writing, including proper use of environments, equations, and citations. - Preserve the overall structure of both documents while making improvements.
prompts.user_prefix:
I am going to give you the main text and supplementary materials of a research paper to correct. Please read both documents carefully.
Here are the LaTeX documents:
<documents> <document name="{PREAMBLE_FILE}"> {PREAMBLE_CONTENT} </document> <document name="{MAIN_FILE}"> {MAIN_CONTENT} </document> <document name="{SUPP_FILE}"> {SUPP_CONTENT} </document> </documents>
prompts.user_request:
Please carefully read through both the main text and supplementary materials, correcting any typos, grammatical errors, formatting inconsistencies, incorrect math, or factual inaccuracies. Pay special attention to:
1. Consistency in notation and terminology between the main text and supplementary materials. 2. Proper cross-referencing between the two documents. 3. Adherence to PRL style and formatting guidelines. 4. Correctness of mathematical equations and factual statements.
Output the corrected versions of both the main text and supplementary materials using the following format:
<latex_documents> <document name="{MAIN_FILE}"> {CORRECTED_MAIN_CONTENT} </document> <document name="{SUPP_FILE}"> {CORRECTED_SUPP_CONTENT} </document> </latex_documents>
